sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Brighton welcome Wolverhampton to the American Express Stadium with the hosts firmly favoured. Brighton sit 8th (50 points) and have been strong at home, while Wolverhampton are 20th (18 points), winless in 6 and without a clean sheet in 7. Model signals a clear home edge and a lower chance of both teams scoring.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Brighton’s last 5: 3 wins, 1 draw, 1 loss; they produced strong performances versus Chelsea (3-0, 2.14 xG) and Liverpool (2-1, 2.17 xG). Wolverhampton’s last 5: 0 wins, 2 draws, 3 losses; they scored 3 and conceded 10, with limited chance creation (≤0.70 xG in 3 of those). The away side have trailed first in 6/6.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: The last 2 meetings at Molineux ended 1-1 and 0-2 to Brighton; Brighton are unbeaten in the last 4 against Wolverhampton. Recent meetings have tilted on territory and shots towards Brighton.

sections.subtitle: Season picture
sections.text: Brighton have 49 scored and 42 conceded, with 9 clean sheets and top-tier pressing (5.09 possessions won in the final third per game, rank 1). Wolverhampton have 25 scored and 63 conceded, pointing to ongoing issues at both ends.

sections.subtitle: Playing styles and key players
sections.text: Brighton’s supply line runs through Pascal Groß and wide threats Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh, while Danny Welbeck is in form (3 goals in 5). Jan Paul van Hecke has regularly excelled in this matchup. Wolverhampton’s brightest outputs have come from Rodrigo Gomes and Hwang Hee-chan, but service and chance quality have been inconsistent.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee John Brooks averages 4.0 yellows per match and few reds (0.13). Brighton average 2.43 yellows per game and head-to-heads have often been card-heavy (more than 4.5 cards in 6/7). Expect around 5 cards and roughly 10 total corners, with Brighton likely to edge the corner count.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Brighton’s recent form, pressing and chance creation against a struggling Wolverhampton defence point to a home win, likely with a clean sheet. A controlled Brighton victory aligns with the model’s strong home bias and the low likelihood of both teams scoring.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Brighton & Hove Albion lead Wolverhampton 2-0 at the break at the American Express Stadium after two early headers (minutes 1 and 5). The hosts controlled territory and tempo, forcing Wolves to defend deep for long spells.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Brighton’s control shows in the numbers: 75% possession, 26 final-third entries, 14 penalty-area entries, 3 shots on target, 3 big chances created (1 missed), expected goals 0.71. They dominated duels (64% won) and aerials (90%). Wolves offered little threat: 25% possession, 13 final-third entries, 5 penalty-area entries, 0 shots on target, expected goals 0.00, and 0 corners.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes
halftimeSections.text: Brighton targeted wide areas and set-pieces. Maxim De Cuyper supplied quality from the left (2 assists, 3 big chances created, 4 key passes), with Lewis Dunk and Jack Hinshelwood attacking deliveries. Danny Welbeck’s pressing helped pin Wolves back, while Carlos Baleba and Jan Paul van Hecke broke up play cleanly. Wolves’ back line struggled to deal with crosses and second balls, and their midfield could not progress play under pressure.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: The opening minutes brought a strong Brighton surge that produced both goals. After a brief consolidation period, the hosts maintained steady attacking pressure through the half, with another pronounced spell just before the interval. Wolves did not sustain any notable attacking spell.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Cards so far: Brighton 1 yellow (Kaoru Mitoma), Wolves 0. Corners: Brighton 3, Wolves 0. Given the game state, Brighton should continue to earn more corners through wide attacks and set-pieces. If Wolves chase the game more aggressively, their card count is likely to rise, but the overall disciplinary profile should remain moderate.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Expect Brighton to manage possession, slow the tempo when needed, and continue to target set-pieces and crosses, where they hold a clear aerial advantage. Wolves need to push their defensive line, support the first pass out, and look for quick transitions into space behind Brighton’s full-backs. More direct running and earlier deliveries could help, but unless their duel and aerial success improves, Brighton’s set-piece threat will remain decisive.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Brighton to see the game out with another goal likely if they maintain delivery quality from wide and dead-ball situations. Next goal prediction: Brighton. Most likely scorer: Danny Welbeck, given his central positioning and first-half involvement. Predicted final score: Brighton 3-0 Wolves.
